{{nihongo|'''Kataoka Shrine'''|片岡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

'''Kataoka Shrine''' (かたおかじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Yoshida, Shizuoka|Q1202789|qid=Q1202789}}, {{ill|Haibara District, Shizuoka|Q1203336|qid=Q1203336}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Q712534|lt=village shrine}}.

=== Overview ===
According to shrine tradition, it is an ancient shrine that was invited from {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}}’s {{ill|Kataoka Shrine (Oji Town)|Q43594918|qid=Q43594918|lt=Kataoka Shrine}}, and it is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}, a divided spirit was invited from {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} in {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}}, after which it came to be known as Sumiyoshi Daimyōjin (Sumiyoshi Shrine). Following the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, Kataoka Shrine was adopted as the official shrine name.

Within the shrine grounds, the boat-shaped object “Sumiyoshi-maru” is displayed.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. Records indicate that the shrine buildings were rebuilt in the 4th year of {{ill|Shōhō|Q1146192|qid=Q1146192}} ({{ill|1647|Q6935|qid=Q6935}}).

In {{ill|1913|Q2080|qid=Q2080}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}), the shrine buildings were renovated from thatched roofing to tiled roofing, based on designs by {{ill|Heisaemon Itō|Q16766564|qid=Q16766564}}, an {{ill|Imperial Household Artist|Q11481067|qid=Q11481067}}.

After the war, the heiden (offering hall) was constructed<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese
  |author = Kataoka Shrine
  |url = http://homepage2.nifty.com/sugao/
  |title = Kataoka Shrine (History and Shrine Tradition)
  |accessdate = 2016-07-31 }}</ref>.

=== Auxiliary shrines ===
The auxiliary and related shrines within the precincts are as follows.

'''Shrines within the grounds'''
* Funatama Shrine
* Hoshinomiya Shrine
* Tsushima Shrine, Inari Shrine, Itsukushima Shrine
* Jūnishin Shrine, Nishinomiya Shrine, Kotohira Shrine
